A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GeneMAN and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Matching relocated and renumbered material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction evaluations, ablations, runtime measurements, and a user study involving 40 participants.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds qualitative comparisons and complex-pose reconstruction examples.

M1.justification: The human-specific diffusion priors, NeRF-to-DMTet geometry pipeline, and latent-then-pixel texture refinement remain unchanged. Revised iteration counts and encoding schedules are experimental settings; no new algorithmic component or loss is introduced.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same enumerated training collection and evaluate single-image reconstruction on CAPE and in-the-wild images. Complex poses, varying body proportions, clothing, and personal belongings were already covered in v1; the additional examples extend evidence within that coverage.

E2.justification: v2 substantially expands qualitative comparator coverage: PIFuHD and PHORHUM join the geometric comparisons in Figures 17–18, corresponding to v1 Figures 13–14. New Figure 13 compares against HumanLRM and IDOL, with HumanLRM results taken from published examples. The quantitative comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported optimization budget changes substantially: DMTet sculpting falls from 10,000 to 3,000 steps, and full positional-encoding exposure moves from 4,000 to 2,000 iterations. Appendix latent-texture optimization changes from 12,000 to 10,000 steps, agreeing with the main text. These reported setting revisions do not establish that retained accuracy experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds targeted qualitative case studies of complex-pose reconstruction in Figures 5, 15, and 16. The existing stage ablations, diffusion-prior ablations, dataset-component ablation, and geometric-ambiguity example are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The user-study sample size and reporting practice remain unchanged.

E6.justification: v2 adds selected qualitative results for the additional comparators and complex poses, while retaining the reconstruction scores, geometric metrics, dataset-ablation values, and user-study results. Runtime reporting changes from 2.35 to 1.42 hours for GeneMAN and from 43 to 2 minutes for SiTH; GeneMAN's sculpting time changes from 65 to 15 minutes alongside its revised optimization budget.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9 and their mathematical reasoning are retained, with no new theorem, proof, or formal assumption. Correcting 'Person' to 'Pearson' and explicitly naming the existing normal-image error as Normal Consistency do not change the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions retain the same claims about template-free reconstruction, human-specific priors, reconstruction quality, and generalization. Added emphasis on complex poses repeats a capability already claimed and illustrated in v1.

C2.justification: The complementary roles of the priors, the SMPL-related evaluation argument, and limitations concerning optimization cost, hands, occlusion, and large objects remain substantively unchanged. New comparator observations and the quantified runtime advantage update results rather than the underlying interpretation or applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: v2 revises optimization schedules and runtime documentation and explains that HumanLRM comparisons use published examples because its code is unavailable. Reproducibility loses some specificity when Appendix B.1 replaces the named ECON keypoint tool with an unspecified off-the-shelf tool. The project link and most implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: New Appendix A substantially expands the discussion beyond human reconstruction to text-to-3D generation and general image-to-3D reconstruction, positioning GeneMAN relative to hybrid-prior approaches. Magic123 and IDOL are newly cited, and HumanLRM's description is refined; HumanLRM itself was already cited under another name in v1.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose edits, condenses comparison descriptions, and corrects ablation and efficiency cross-references. It adds a related-work appendix section and moves references after the supplementary material, while retaining the main narrative and section organization.

P2.justification: The visual presentation is substantially revised: Figure 1 is redesigned, four figures are added, geometric comparison plates gain two comparator columns, and v1 Tables 1–2 are merged into v2 Table 1. Existing figures are reordered or relocated; the seven extended qualitative comparison plates are retained as Figures 19–25.

improvement.justification: v2 provides useful additional support for generalization through relevant qualitative baselines and complex-pose examples, expands research context, and improves consistency between the reported optimization schedules and runtime breakdown. The gain is limited because the quantitative reconstruction evidence is unchanged and the additions remain primarily qualitative. Removing the named keypoint extractor introduces a small reproducibility loss.
